Name: Notice and pre-approval of invoicing requirements and changes to such requirements.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to notice and pre-approval of invoicing requirements and changes to such requirements

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Contracts

Summary: This bill would require an agency to provide notice to a contractor, when the agency and contractor enter into a contract, of what will be required when later submitting invoices to that agency. All such requirements would need to be pre-approved by the City Chief Procurement Officer (CCPO). An agency would be allowed to make changes to these requirements only after receiving approval for those changes from the CCPO. The CCPO would be required to report annually to the Mayor and the Speaker of the Council on compliance with this law.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to notice and pre-approval of invoicing requirements and changes to such requirements

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Chapter 1 of title 6 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 6-152 to read as follows:
§ 6-152 Uniform invoice process. a. Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
Contractor. The term “contractor" means any person that enters into a contract with an agency.
Invoicing requirement. The term “invoicing requirement” means any requirement imposed on a contractor regarding invoicing or requesting payment for services performed or costs incurred.
b. 1. When entering into a contract, an agency shall include in such contract or notify the contractor in writing of all invoicing requirements applicable to such contract. 
2. No agency may impose an invoicing requirement, modify an existing invoicing requirement, or request additional information or documentation from a contractor in connection with any invoice or request for payment that was not specified in an existing invoicing requirement, without approval from the city chief procurement officer.
c. No later than one year after the effective date of the local law that added this section and annually thereafter, the city chief procurement officer shall report to the mayor and the speaker of the council on agency compliance with this section.
§ 2. This local law takes effect 120 days after enactment.
